reading.body:
Clay White is named on 5 Lobbying Disclosure Act filings about AI, all filed through one lobbying firm for a single client, THE AI POLICY NETWORK INC.

The record is narrow and concentrated. Five filings, one firm, one client. The 14 bills named across those filings are the substance of the disclosure: S 4456, S 1633, HR 3919, HR 3460, S 2296, HR 2385, S 2938, S 4216, S 1792, HR 9477, S 4113, HR 5885, HR 6875, S 3108, and S 2615, each tied to a filing dated 2025 or later. The disclosed prior government positions are congressional staff roles for Chris Stewart and Jason Chaffetz, which the Lobbying Disclosure Act requires filers to list for twenty years back.

For AI specifically, this is the legislative layer of the buildout rather than the physical one. Compute, buildings, and power determine what can be trained and served. Lobbying records like this one show which bills touching AI are being worked and by whom, which is upstream of the rules that shape permitting, procurement, and deployment. The data does not connect any filing to a data center, a grid interconnection, or a power contract, so no claim about physical infrastructure can be drawn from it.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. It records that a name appears on filings and which bills those filings name. It does not say what position was advocated, whether the advocacy succeeded, how much was spent, or whether any bill became law. The page's own note is that it draws no conclusion about the person, and the summary flags that a different lobbyist shares the name.
